x: Also included in the programme was a 2 mile Walk, which was won by Eric Hall, with our new member, Demmon, in second place. It was pleasing to see such a good turn-out by our lads, and we hope that they keep up the good work throughout the season.

All the handicap team prizes stopped over our side of the water as Surrey W.C. took 1st place, our "B" team (Demmon, Middleton Wilson,Doubleday) were 2nd and the "A" Team (Hall,Checkley,Eglington McMullen) were 3rd.
All the good peerformances were too numerous to give in detail, but briefly Hall, Phillips, Demmon, Middleton, Eglington Newson and Scamell all beat the hour and were awarded their 7 miles badges.
The next three places were filled by Surrey and then three more for us - Guilmant, Eglington and Demmon. Scoring 20 a side, we won by 397 points to 423.

Not disheartened, the other lads walked exceptionally well and with Eric Hall 11th, George Checkley 16th, Len Demmon 18th and Bob Newson 28th we totalled 68 points to finish 3rd to Woodford Green 21 points, with Met.
A nice exhibition of packing by Len Demmon 16th, Bob Newson 18th and George Checkley 19th, with a tolal of 53 points, once again secured us 3rd place.
Our other lads had been going well and at 5 miles Newson was 13th, Demmon (later disqualified) 16th and Ted Smith 31st, with the remainder of the lads moving up well.
After Mr. "Tonv Curtis" Demmon had finished playing the wicked uncle stuff witn the Wiltshire young ladies, we decided to pass time by drinking tea in the local snack bar.
